lines.trans: Oh no! Ernesto, Clara, we have an emergency in the kitchen!
Please do not say the word emergency before my morning coffee!
The delivery van has a flat tyre. Look in the fridge!
A tiny splash of milk, two eggs, and no butter at all!
Eight hungry guests are coming down the stairs at seven thirty!
My bread is already in the oven, at least.
Give me a bag and cash! The corner market opens at seven.

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Can you run there and back in ten minutes?
You will see! Tell me exactly what to buy.
Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!
Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!
Hold the fort, I am already heading out the door!

lines.trans: Can you run there and back in ten minutes?
You will see! Tell me exactly what to buy.
Three bottles of milk, twenty eggs, butter, cheese, and red apples!
Here is fifty euros from the cash box. Bring back the receipt!
Hold the fort, I am already heading out the door!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.text: ¡Ay, casi olvido el paraguas!
examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!

examples.text: ¡Ay, qué susto me has dado!
examples.trans: Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Una urgencia = an emergency.

examples.text: La urgencia está aquí.
examples.trans: The emergency is here.

examples.text: Vemos las urgencias desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the emergencies from the door.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.text: La cocina está aquí.
examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.text: El favor está aquí.
examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Ni una palabra = not a word.

examples.text: La palabra está aquí.
examples.trans: The word is here.

examples.text: Vemos las palabras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the words from the door.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Plural los cafés (two coffees = dos cafés).

examples.text: El café está aquí.
examples.trans: The coffee is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cafés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coffees from the door.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.

examples.text: ¡Hasta mañana a las ocho!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: Small commercial van.

examples.text: La furgoneta está aquí.
examples.trans: The delivery van is here.

examples.text: Vemos las furgonetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the delivery vans from the door.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Morning bread or parcel delivery.

examples.text: El reparto es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The delivery is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el reparto.
examples.trans: We talk about the delivery.

meanings.note: Suitcase wheel, bicycle wheel, or round boiler wheel.

examples.text: La rueda está aquí.
examples.trans: The wheel is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ruedas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the wheels from the door.

meanings.note: Rueda pinchada = flat tyre.

examples.text: Es una pieza pinchada.
examples.trans: It is a punctured piece.

examples.text: La furgoneta del reparto tiene una rueda pinchada. ¡Mirad la nevera!
examples.trans: The delivery van has a flat tyre. Look in the fridge!

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for the kitchen refrigerator.

examples.text: La nevera está aquí.
examples.trans: The fridge is here.

examples.text: Vemos las neveras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the fridges from the door.

meanings.note: Un poco de mantequilla = a little butter.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco de miel en el té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little honey in your tea?

examples.text: Quedan pocos minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: Few minutes remain until noon.

meanings.note: Café con leche = white coffee.

examples.text: La leche es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The milk is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la leche.
examples.trans: We talk about the milk.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Huevos revueltos = scrambled eggs.

examples.text: El huevo está aquí.
examples.trans: The egg is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huevos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eggs from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.text: Tranquilo, no pasa nada.
examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.

examples.text: No queda nada de mantequilla.
examples.trans: There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Spread on warm morning toast.

examples.text: La mantequilla es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The butter is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la mantequilla.
examples.trans: We talk about the butter.

meanings.note: Las ocho = eight o'clock.

examples.text: Abrimos la puerta a las ocho.
examples.trans: We open the door at eight.

examples.text: La posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: The guesthouse has eight rooms.

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.text: El cliente está aquí.
examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in singular when article is used (tengo mucha hambre).

examples.text: El hambre es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The hunger is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el hambre.
examples.trans: We talk about the hunger.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.text: La escalera está aquí.
examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.text: Es una pieza media.
examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: El pan es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The bread is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el pan.
examples.trans: We talk about the bread.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.

examples.text: ¡Ya voy con las llaves!
examples.trans: Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Del horno = out of the oven.

examples.text: El horno está aquí.
examples.trans: The oven is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hornos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ovens from the door.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.text: Son las ocho menos diez.
examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Shopping or paper/cloth bag.

examples.text: La bolsa está aquí.
examples.trans: The bag is here.

examples.text: Vemos las bolsas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bags from the door.

meanings.note: Pagar en efectivo means 'to pay in cash'.

examples.text: El efectivo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The cash is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el efectivo.
examples.trans: We talk about the cash.

meanings.note: Covered food market in a Spanish neighbourhood.

examples.text: El mercado está aquí.
examples.trans: The market is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mercados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the markets from the door.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.text: ¿Puedo ver la etiqueta otra vez?
examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

volver.gloss: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

examples.text: Vuelvo en cinco minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in five minutes.

examples.text: Volvió a sonreír enseguida.
examples.trans: He smiled again right away.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para empezar.
examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.

examples.text: Su recepción merece un diez.
examples.trans: Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.text: El minuto está aquí.
examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Compro pan caliente en la esquina.
examples.trans: I buy warm bread on the corner.

examples.text: Ayer compramos seis limones amarillos.
examples.trans: Yesterday we bought six yellow lemons.

meanings.note: Formed from exacta + -mente.

examples.text: Sabe exactamente igual que antes.
examples.trans: It tastes exactly the same as before.

examples.text: Son las doce exactamente.
examples.trans: It is twelve o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Glass or plastic bottle.

examples.text: La botella está aquí.
examples.trans: The bottle is here.

examples.text: Vemos las botellas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bottles from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Mide exactamente veinte milímetros.
examples.trans: It measures exactly twenty millimetres.

examples.text: Son las once y veinte.
examples.trans: It is eleven twenty.

meanings.note: Queso manchego or breakfast cheese.

examples.text: El queso está aquí.
examples.trans: The cheese is here.

examples.text: Vemos los quesos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cheeses from the door.

meanings.note: Means both 'apple' and a square block of city buildings.

examples.text: La manzana está aquí.
examples.trans: The apple is here.

examples.text: Vemos las manzanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the apples from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.text: Es una pieza roja.
examples.trans: It is a red piece.

examples.text: ¡Dígales que la mía tiene una cinta roja en el bolsillo de arriba!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Son las once y cincuenta.
examples.trans: It is eleven fifty.

examples.text: El libro tiene cincuenta páginas.
examples.trans: The book has fifty pages.

meanings.note: Currency of Spain.

examples.text: Un café con leche y dos churros calientes cuestan apenas tres euros.
examples.trans: A coffee with milk and two hot churros cost barely three euros.

examples.text: El billete de autobús hasta el centro histórico cuesta solo dos euros.
examples.trans: The bus ticket to the historic center costs only two euros.

meanings.note: Caja de herramientas = toolbox; la caja also means the cash register/box.

examples.text: La caja está aquí.
examples.trans: The box is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cajas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the boxs from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: traigo, traje; future traeré.

examples.text: Ahora mismo le traigo una cuchara.
examples.trans: I will bring you a spoon right now.

examples.text: Ayer trajo flores del mercado.
examples.trans: Yesterday she brought flowers from the market.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Recibimos a los huéspedes con té.
examples.trans: We welcome guests with tea.

examples.text: Esta mañana recibí una carta certificada.
examples.trans: This morning I received a registered letter.

cuidar.gloss: to look after; to take care of

meanings.en: to look after; to take care of
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Cuidamos cada detalle de la casa.
examples.trans: We look after every detail of the house.

examples.text: Ella cuida las plantas del balcón.
examples.trans: She tends the balcony plants.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.text: ¡Hasta pronto y buen viaje!
examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.
